analysis.title: Americas Transportation: The Monthly Mosaic: October 2026
key_insights: US ISM Manufacturing was 55.5 in October, up about 1 point from September and the tenth straight month above 50. ISM New Orders was also 55.5.

ISM New Orders (55.5) minus ISM Inventories (51.4) gives a +4.1 spread. GS notes ISM inventory spread has directionally tracked CASS freight volumes, so higher new orders could foreshadow freight tailwinds.

China manufacturing PMI stayed expansionary in October at 52.0, slightly below September. Eurozone manufacturing PMI was 52.7 (52.9 in September). Mexico manufacturing PMI turned contractionary in October.

Logistics Managers Index overall inventory levels expanded faster in October than September, approaching Covid-peak ordering levels. Retail and B2B inventories both accelerated, possibly reflecting stocking ahead of the holidays.
Dry van spot truck rates (ex-fuel surcharge) averaged +28% YoY and +7% MoM in October, outperforming historical seasonality by 1140bps after muted August and September.

YoY spot rate growth was +27%, +22% and +28% in August, September and October. GS attributes part of this to limited capacity and driver pool from tighter CDL restrictions and English language enforcement.
Assuming normal seasonality, GS sees YoY spot rate growth of about +36% in November and about +21% in December.
Dry Van Market Demand Index averaged about +80% YoY in October, with truck availability -31% YoY and load availability +25% YoY.
CASS Truckload Linehaul Index (contract rate proxy) was +10% YoY, the second straight month of double-digit growth (September +11%). Contract rates could improve further if spot rates stay elevated.

Preliminary seasonally adjusted net Class 8 truck orders were about 10.6k in October, -38% MoM and -45% YoY, well below the 10-year monthly average of about 25k. This followed about seven months of above-replacement ordering through July.
Ocean container rates (China/East Asia to NA West Coast) were +370% YoY on average in October versus +309% in September.
Air freight rates from Shanghai to US West Coast were +8% MoM and +42% YoY in October (+34% YoY in September).
Big Three West Coast ports inbound loaded containers were +23% YoY in September, +35% versus 2019 levels.
Rail volumes in October: total Class 1 traffic +6.3% YoY, intermodal +8.8%, economically sensitive carloads +7.8%, industrial carloads +6.0%, coal -0.9%.

Class 8 backlog-to-build ratio was about 7 months in September, in line with the 10-year average. Cancellations were about 4% of gross orders versus an 11% 10-year average. Active truck utilization was 99.9%.

GS thinks trucking may be moving past the cycle bottom into recovery and expects more upside over the next twelve months than rails. It stays positive on parcel for fast-cycle logistics and margin recovery, but says economic and trade policy uncertainty could keep transports under pressure.

risk_factors: Uncertainty around economic activity and trade policy could keep transports under pressure.
Class 8 net orders at 10.6k in October (-45% YoY) are well below the 10-year average, a sign of weak fleet investment.
Mexico manufacturing PMI turned contractionary in October.
Auto carloads were -2.0% YoY in September and coal carloads -0.9% YoY in October.

tension_points.bull_case: Spot rates are +28% YoY and contract rates +10% YoY, with truck availability -31% YoY and driver capacity limited by CDL restrictions. GS sees trucking past the cycle bottom with more upside than rails.
tension_points.bear_case: Class 8 net orders fell 38% MoM to 10.6k, well below the 10-year average of about 25k, and economic and trade policy uncertainty could keep transports under pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Spot rates failing to follow the normal seasonal path to about +36% YoY in November and +21% in December.
